shared_elements: large upright freestanding stone monolith carved in low relief
broader upper block over a narrower lower shaft
relief organised in stacked horizontal registers
horizontal band of repeated short vertical strokes / row of similar motifs at the top
elongated sinuous forms running down the shaft
raised outlined bands framing zones of the surface
justification: Both are tall monolithic slabs whose relief is organised into a broad upper zone containing a row of repeated motifs, separated by a horizontal banded divider from a lower shaft bearing larger isolated figures and a disc, which is a fairly specific shared compositional scheme. The rendering differs strongly, however: A is a dark, heavily weathered stone with soft, rounded, largely abstract swellings and no clearly legible animals, while B is pale, crisply cut and populated by recognisable profile creatures, so the resemblance is structural rather than stylistic.
